formation: 시각을 나타낼 때 시간(시)은 고유어 수로, 분은 한자어 수로 읽으며, 때를 나타내는 명사 뒤에는 조사 에를 붙임.
meaning_en: telling the time (hours are read with native Korean numbers, minutes with Sino-Korean numbers)
meaning_zh: 表示时间（小时用固有词数词，分钟用汉字词数词）。
meaning_ko: 시각을 말할 때 시는 고유어 수, 분은 한자어 수로 읽는 표현.

examples.english: What time is it now?
It's 9:10 in the morning.
What time do you wake up?
I wake up at 7:00 in the morning.

notes: 오전 and 오후 literally mean 'before noon' and 'after noon', but in Korean 오전 typically means the morning hours and 오후 the afternoon hours; time can also be subdivided into 새벽, 아침, 점심, 저녁, and 밤.

formation: 동사/형용사 어간이 모음으로 끝나면 -ㅂ니다(의문형 -ㅂ니까?), 자음으로 끝나면 -습니다(의문형 -습니까?)를 붙임.
meaning_en: present tense formal polite style (declarative and interrogative)
meaning_zh: 现在时正式敬语体，主要用于正式或公开场合。
meaning_ko: 격식체(합쇼체) 현재 시제로, 주로 공식적이거나 공적인 상황에서 사용하는 표현.

examples.english: Good evening.
This is the 9 o'clock news.
Do you have any questions?
What's your opinion of this?
I think it's good.

formation: 어간의 끝 모음이 ㅏ나 ㅗ이면 -아요를, 그 외의 모음이면 -어요를 붙이고, 하다로 끝나면 해요가 됨. 이다 뒤에는 모음으로 끝나면 예요, 자음으로 끝나면 이에요를 씀.
meaning_en: present tense informal polite style (declarative and interrogative)
meaning_zh: 现在时非正式敬语体，日常口语中最常用的礼貌表达。
meaning_ko: 일상에서 가장 많이 쓰는 두루 높임말(해요체) 현재 시제 표현.

examples.english: Does it taste good?
Yes, it tastes good.
Where are you going?
I'm going to school.
I love you, Carol.

formation: 어간의 끝 모음이 ㅏ나 ㅗ이면 -았어요를, 그 외의 모음이면 -었어요를 붙이고, 하다로 끝나면 했어요가 됨.
meaning_en: past tense (informal polite style)
meaning_zh: 过去时，表示过去发生的动作或状态。
meaning_ko: 과거에 일어난 일이나 상태를 나타내는 과거 시제 표현.

examples.english: The baby was born on March 5, 1981.
I graduated from college in February 2004.
We got married last year.
What did you do yesterday?
I studied.

notes: While the past tense of 주다 can be written either as 주었어요 or 줬어요, and the past tense of 보다 can be written either as 보았어요 or 봤어요, the past tense of 오다 is written only as 왔어요, not 오았어요.

formation: 동사 어간이 모음으로 끝나면 -ㄹ 거예요를, 자음으로 끝나면 -을 거예요를 붙임.
meaning_en: will / going to do (future plan or intention)
meaning_zh: 将要……；打算……（表将来的计划或意图）。
meaning_ko: 앞으로의 계획이나 의지를 나타내는 미래 시제 표현.

examples.english: I'll buy a car two years from now.
I'll go fishing this weekend.
I'll visit China during my vacation.
When will you return to your hometown?
I'll return next year.

formation: 동사 어간 + -고 있다
meaning_en: is -ing (with wear/put-on verbs, expresses a state resulting from a completed action that continues to the present)
meaning_zh: 正……着（与穿戴类动词连用，表动作结果持续到现在的状态）
meaning_ko: 입다, 신다, 쓰다, 끼다, 벗다처럼 옷이나 물건을 착용하거나 벗는 동사와 함께 쓰여, 행동의 결과가 지금까지 그 상태로 이어짐을 나타내는 표현이다.

examples.english: I'm wearing a necklace and earrings.
I'm wearing a blouse.
I'm wearing a skirt.
I'm wearing boots.
I'm wearing glasses.
She's wearing a red dress.

examples.korean: 우리 집은 추워요. 그래서 양말을 신고 있어요.
examples.english: Our house is cold. So I'm wearing socks.
examples.chinese: 我们家很冷，所以穿着袜子。

notes: The same meaning can also be expressed by using the past tense form -았/었어요 to indicate a state of completed action (e.g. 치마를 입고 있어요 = 치마를 입었어요).

formation: 어간의 끝 모음이 ㅏ나 ㅗ이면 -았었어요를, 그 외의 모음이면 -었었어요를 붙이고, 하다로 끝나면 했었어요가 됨.
meaning_en: past perfect — a past situation that is no longer the case or is disconnected from the present ('used to', 'had done')
meaning_zh: 曾经……（表过去发生但现已不再持续、与现在断开的状态或事情）。
meaning_ko: 과거에 있었던 일이 지금은 계속되지 않거나 현재와 단절되어 있음을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I have been to the U.S.
I had lived in China.
My father was overweight.

examples.korean: 작년에는 담배를 피웠었어요. 그렇지만 지금은 안 피워요.
examples.english: I smoked last year, but I don't smoke now.
examples.chinese: 去年抽过烟，但现在不抽了。

examples.english: There were many people there in the summer.

notes: -았/었어요 simply states that something occurred in the past or that a past state has remained, while -았/었었어요 emphasizes that the past situation is no longer the case or is disconnected from the present.

pattern: N이/가 아니다, N이/가 없다, N을/를 모르다
formation: 단어를 부정할 때 이다 → 아니다, 있다 → 없다, 알다 → 모르다로 바꿈. 아니다는 이/가 아니다 형태로 쓰임.
meaning_en: word negation — negating a word (이다→아니다, 있다→없다, 알다→모르다)
meaning_zh: 单词否定（把 이다 变为 아니다、있다 变为 없다、알다 变为 모르다）。
meaning_ko: 문장 전체가 아니라 단어를 부정하여 부정문을 만드는 표현.

examples.english: She is Korean.
She is not Korean.
I don't have any money.
I don't know Korean.
No, he's not a student. He's a teacher.

notes: 아니다 is written in the form 이/가 아니다, but when used in the spoken form, 이/가 is often omitted.

formation: 동사나 형용사 앞에 안을 붙이거나, 어간 뒤에 -지 않아요를 붙임.
meaning_en: negation 'not' — negating an action or state
meaning_zh: 否定：不……（在动词/形容词前加 안，或在词干后加 -지 않다）。
meaning_ko: 동사나 형용사에 안을 붙이거나 -지 않다를 붙여 부정하는 표현.

examples.korean: 저는 오징어를 안 먹어요. (= 저는 오징어를 먹지 않아요.)
examples.english: I don't eat squid.

examples.korean: 그 구두는 안 예뻐요. (= 그 구두는 예쁘지 않아요.)
examples.english: Those shoes aren't pretty.

examples.korean: 방이 안 넓어요. (= 방이 넓지 않아요.)
examples.english: The room is not spacious.
No. I don't eat meat.
No, on Saturdays, I don't go to work.

notes: Although 안 and -지 않다 can be used in declarative and interrogative sentences, they cannot be used in imperative or propositive sentences (e.g. 안 가십시오 (X) / 가지 마십시오 (O)). Also, 좋아하다 and 싫어하다 are written as 안 좋아하다/좋아하지 않다, not 좋아 안 하다.

formation: 동사 앞에 못을 붙이거나, 어간 뒤에 -지 못해요를 붙임.
meaning_en: cannot — inability or impossibility due to external factors
meaning_zh: 不能……（表没有能力或因外部情况而无法做某事）。
meaning_ko: 능력이 없거나 외부 상황 때문에 어떤 행동을 할 수 없음을 나타내는 표현.

examples.korean: 저는 수영을 못해요. (= 저는 수영하지 못해요.)
examples.english: I can't swim.

examples.korean: 오늘은 술을 못 마셔요. (= 오늘은 술을 마시지 못해요.)
examples.english: I can't drink today.

examples.korean: 저는 노래를 못 불러요. (= 저는 노래를 부르지 못해요.)
examples.english: I can't sing.

examples.korean: 아니요, 운전 못해요. 운전을 안 배웠어요.
examples.english: No, I can't drive. I never learned how.
examples.chinese: 不，我不会开车。没学过开车。

examples.english: My teeth hurt, so I can't eat.

notes: 안 (-지 않다) combines with both verbs and adjectives and expresses not doing something regardless of ability or external conditions, whereas 못 (-지 못하다) combines normally with verbs only and is used when one is unable, or it is impossible, to do something.

formation: 받침이 있으면 이, 받침이 없으면 가를 붙임.
meaning_en: subject particle (marks the subject; also emphasizes the subject or introduces new information)
meaning_zh: 主格助词（标记主语，也用于强调主语或引出新信息）。
meaning_ko: 문장의 주어임을 나타내는 주격 조사.

examples.english: The weather is nice.
A long time ago, there was a princess.
There's Jaejun coming (this way).
Joel eats bread.
My stomach hurts.

notes: When 가 is added to 나, 저, and 누구, they combine as follows: 나 + 가 → 내가, 저 + 가 → 제가, 누구 + 가 → 누가.

formation: 받침이 있으면 은, 받침이 없으면 는을 붙임.
meaning_en: topic particle (marks the topic; also used for contrast or for known/old information)
meaning_zh: 主题助词（标记话题，也用于对比或已知信息）。
meaning_ko: 문장의 화제(주제)를 나타내는 보조사.

examples.korean: 형은 키가 커요. 동생은 키가 작아요.
examples.english: My older brother is tall. My younger brother is short.
examples.chinese: 哥哥个子高，弟弟个子矮。

examples.korean: 부디 씨는 운동을 잘해요. 그렇지만 공부는 못해요.
examples.english: Budi is good at sports. Studying, however, is not his forte.
examples.chinese: 布迪擅长运动，但学习不行。

examples.english: I'm Korean.
Richard is 29 years old.
My father is an office worker, and my mother is a teacher.
examples.chinese: 父亲是公司职员，母亲是老师。

notes: When comparing or contrasting two things, 은/는 can be attached not only to subjects but also to objects or other parts of the sentence.

formation: 받침이 있으면 을, 받침이 없으면 를을 붙임.
meaning_en: object particle (marks the object of a verb)
meaning_zh: 宾格助词（标记动词的宾语）。
meaning_ko: 목적어임을 나타내는 목적격 조사.

examples.english: Budi watches a movie.
Dad reads the newspaper.
Yoko listens to music.
I like soccer.
I'll meet my girlfriend.

notes: When 을/를 is omitted from verbs like 공부를 하다, 수영을 하다, 운동을 하다, and 산책을 하다, the form becomes shortened to a single one-word form: 공부하다, 수영하다, 운동하다, and 산책하다. Also, 무엇을 해요? can be shortened to 뭐 해요? in conversation.

formation: 받침이 있으면 과/이랑, 받침이 없으면 와/랑을 쓰고, 하고는 받침에 상관없이 씀.
meaning_en: 'and' — listing things or people; also 'together with' (와/과 mainly in writing, (이)랑/하고 in conversation)
meaning_zh: ……和……（并列事物或人；와/과 多用于书面，(이)랑/하고 多用于口语；也可表‘和……一起’）。
meaning_ko: 여러 사물이나 사람을 나열할 때 쓰는 접속 조사.

examples.english: I like watermelons and strawberries.
Yesterday, I bought a bag and a hat.
I'll have a hamburger and coke, please.

examples.korean: 내일 친구하고 같이 영화를 볼 거예요.
examples.english: I plan to see a movie together with my friend tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 明天要和朋友一起看电影。

examples.english: I like cold noodles and gimbap.

notes: When listing things, (이)랑 and 하고 can be added to the final noun in the list, but 와/과 cannot. Although 와/과, (이)랑, and 하고 can all be used similarly, they cannot be mixed within the same sentence.

formation: 명사 뒤에 의를 붙여 앞의 명사가 뒤의 명사를 소유함을 나타냄. 회화에서는 자주 생략됨.
meaning_en: possessive particle ('s / of)
meaning_zh: 所有格助词，表示‘……的’。
meaning_ko: 앞의 명사가 뒤의 명사를 소유함을 나타내는 관형격 조사.

examples.korean: 이것은 웨슬리의 책이에요. (= 이것은 웨슬리 책이에요.)
examples.english: This is Wesley's book.

examples.korean: 이분은 부디 씨의 선생님입니다. (= 이분은 부디 씨 선생님입니다.)
examples.english: This is Budi's teacher.

examples.korean: 제 이름은 요코입니다. (= 저의 이름은 요코입니다.)
examples.english: My name is Yoko.
It's Jaejun's umbrella.
It's Jason's mother.

notes: When referring to a group with which one is associated (home, family, company, country, or school), it is common to use 우리/저희 in place of 저/내. When showing respect to the listener, 저희, the humble form of 우리, is used.

formation: 명사 뒤에 에를 붙여 행동이 향하는 방향이나 사람·사물이 있는 위치를 나타냄.
meaning_en: to / in / on — direction of movement or the location of a person or thing
meaning_zh: 表示方向（往……）或位置（在……）。
meaning_ko: 행동이 향하는 방향이나 사람·사물이 있는 위치를 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: My friend is coming to Korea.
My little brother goes to school.
I go back to my hometown next month.
The dog is on the sofa.
I'm going to the department store.

notes: 에 cannot be added to 그제 (그저께), 어제 (어저께), 오늘, 내일, 모레, or 언제. When more than one noun representing time is used in a sentence, 에 is added only to the final noun.

formation: 장소 명사 뒤에 에서를 붙여 동작이나 행동이 일어나는 장소를 나타냄.
meaning_en: at / in — the place where an action occurs
meaning_zh: 表示动作发生的地点（在……）。
meaning_ko: 어떤 행동이나 동작이 일어나는 장소를 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I study at school.
I saw a movie at the theater.
I'll eat at the cafeteria.
I live in Seoul.
I met my friend at Myeongdong.

notes: When used before the verb 살다, the particles 에 and 에서 can both be used with very little difference in meaning.

formation: 명사 + 에서 + 명사 + 까지 / 명사 + 부터 + 명사 + 까지
meaning_en: from ... to ... (range of locations); from ... until ... (range of times)
meaning_zh: 从……到……（表地点或时间的范围）
meaning_ko: 어떤 행동이나 사건이 미치는 장소적·시간적 범위를 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I walked home from school.
How long does it take to get from Seoul to Busan?
examples.chinese: 从首尔到釜山需要多长时间？

examples.english: I work from 9:00 A.M. until 5:00 P.M.
examples.chinese: 我从上午9点工作到下午5点。

examples.english: Is it far from here to school?
Yes, on Saturdays, it's open from 10 A.M. until 4 P.M.
examples.chinese: 是的，周六从上午10点开放到下午4点。

formation: 명사(사람·동물) + 에게/한테
meaning_en: to (a person or animal); marks the recipient or target of an action
meaning_zh: 给……；向……（表动作的接受者或对象，只用于人或动物）
meaning_ko: 사람이나 동물을 나타내는 명사에 붙어 그 명사가 행동의 받는 사람이나 대상임을 나타내는 표현.

examples.korean: 재준 씨가 캐럴 씨에게 선물을 줍니다.
examples.english: Jaejun gives a present to Carol.
The teacher teaches Korean to the students.
My little sister feeds the dog.
Who are you writing a letter to?
I'm writing a letter to my friend back home.

notes: When the target of the action is someone of higher social status to whom the speaker must show respect, the honorific 께 is used in place of 에게/한테 and 드리다 in place of 주다 (e.g. 나는 할아버지께 선물을 드렸습니다). When receiving or learning something from another person, 에게서 받다/배우다 or 한테서 받다/배우다 is used, and 서 can be omitted (에게/한테 받다/배우다); for a person of higher status, 께 is used in place of 에게서/한테서.

formation: 명사 + 도
meaning_en: also / too (adds a subject or object to one already mentioned)
meaning_zh: 也；还（把主语或宾语添加到已提到的事物上）
meaning_ko: 앞에서 언급한 것에 더하여 주어나 목적어를 나열하거나 추가할 때 쓰는 표현.

examples.korean: 무쿨 씨는 인도 사람이에요. 그리고 친구도 인도 사람이에요.
examples.english: Mukul is Indian. And his friend is also Indian.
examples.chinese: 穆库尔是印度人。他的朋友也是印度人。

examples.korean: 아버지는 키가 커요. 그리고 저도 키가 커요.
examples.english: My father is tall. And I am tall, too.
examples.chinese: 爸爸个子高。我也个子高。

examples.korean: 왕징 씨는 사과를 좋아해요. 그리고 딸기도 좋아해요.
examples.english: Wang Jing likes apples. And she likes strawberries, too.
examples.chinese: 王静喜欢苹果。也喜欢草莓。

examples.korean: 비빔밥을 먹을 거예요. 그리고 된장찌개도 먹을 거예요.
examples.english: I'll have bibimbap. And I'll have doenjang stew, too.
examples.chinese: 我要吃拌饭。还要吃大酱汤。

examples.english: I study Korean. And I also learn taekwondo.

formation: 명사 + 만
meaning_en: only / just (choosing one thing to the exclusion of others)
meaning_zh: 只；仅（排除其他，只选择某一个）
meaning_ko: 다른 것은 제외하고 하나만 선택함을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: Today, only Carol came to school.
examples.chinese: 今天只有卡罗尔来学校了。

examples.korean: 댄 씨는 야채는 안 먹어요. 고기만 먹어요.
examples.english: Dane doesn't eat vegetables. He only eats meat.
Please wait just five minutes.
Only Budi hasn't arrived.
Just sugar, please.

notes: 만 can be used either in place of the particles 이/가, 은/는, and 을/를, or together with them; when used together, 만 comes first, followed by 이, 은, or 을, forming 만이, 만은, and 만을. With particles other than 이/가, 은/는, and 을/를, 만 comes after the particle, forming 에서만, 에게만, and 까지만.

formation: 명사 + 밖에 + 부정 표현(안, 못, 없다, 모르다)
meaning_en: only / nothing but (used with a following negative; the amount is less than expected)
meaning_zh: 只；仅；除了……之外没有（必须与后面的否定形式连用）
meaning_ko: 다른 가능성 없이 오직 그것뿐임을 나타내며, 반드시 뒤에 부정 표현이 오는 표현.

examples.english: There's only one apple left.
There's nothing but milk in the refrigerator.
I only received one present.
It's difficult, so I could only read five pages.
I invited 30 people, but only 20 came.
examples.chinese: 我邀请了30人，可是只来了20人。

notes: 밖에 is always followed by a negative form (안, 못, 없다, 몰라요), but it cannot be followed by 아니다, nor by imperative or propositive forms (10분밖에 기다리지 맙시다 is wrong; 10분만 기다립시다 is correct). Unlike 만, which can be used in both positive and negative sentences, 밖에 is used in negative sentences only.

formation: 명사 + (으)로 (받침이 없거나 'ㄹ'로 끝나면 로, 받침이 있으면 으로)
meaning_en: to / toward (direction); by / with / using (means of transport, tool, or material)
meaning_zh: 向……；朝……（表方向）；乘……；用……（表手段、工具、材料）
meaning_ko: 방향이나 수단·도구·재료를 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: Please go to the right from here.
We go from Seoul to Jeju Island by airplane.
examples.chinese: 从首尔到济州岛坐飞机去。

examples.english: I cut the paper with scissors.
We made jam from peanuts.
This candy is made of rice.
examples.chinese: 这个点心是用大米做的。

notes: When a means of transport is expressed by a verb instead of a noun, -아/어서 is added to the verb, as in 걸어서, 뛰어서, 달려서, 운전해서, and 수영해서 (e.g. 학교에서 집까지 걸어서 가요). Also note the difference between 차로 왔어요 (traveled by car, whether driving or as a passenger) and 운전해서 왔어요 (the subject actually drove the car), and between -(으)로 가다 (focus on direction) and -에 가다 (focus on destination).

formation: 명사 + (이)나 (받침이 없으면 나, 받침이 있으면 이나)
meaning_en: or (choosing one of two or more listed nouns)
meaning_zh: 或者；……或……（在并列的两个以上名词中选择一个）
meaning_ko: 둘 이상 나열된 명사 중 하나를 선택함을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: In the mornings, I eat bread or rice.
I'm thirsty. Please give me some water or juice.
examples.chinese: 我口渴。请给我水或果汁。

examples.english: I want to go to Jeju Island or Mt. Seorak during the school vacation.
examples.chinese: 放假想去济州岛或雪岳山。

examples.english: I plan to buy some shoes or a bag.
Please ask instructor Lee or instructor Kim.

notes: When (이)나 is added to a subject or object, the subject/object particle is omitted, leaving only (이)나 in place of 이/가 or 을/를 (어머니나 아버지가 요리해요). With the particles 에, 에서, and 에게, (이)나 may be used alone with the first word(s) while 에/에서/에게 is used with the final word, or (이)나 may be combined with them to form 에나, 에서나, 에게나, though using (이)나 alone is more natural. While 밖에 indicates that a number or amount is less than expected or doesn't meet a general standard, (이)나 indicates that it is more than expected or exceeds a general standard. The same quantity can be viewed either way depending on the perspective (e.g. 우리는 아이가 네 명밖에 없어요 vs 네 명이나 있어요?).

formation: 명사 + 쯤
meaning_en: about / around (approximate number, quantity, or time)
meaning_zh: 大约；左右（表数量、时间等大致估计）
meaning_ko: 수, 양, 시간 등을 대략적으로 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: About 20 people came to the party.
I arrived at the airport around 1 o'clock.
These days, tomatoes cost about 3,000 won.
How's around 1 o'clock?
It takes me about 30 minutes by bus.
examples.chinese: 坐公交车大约需要30分钟。

notes: When referring to approximate prices, 'Noun쯤 하다' is used more often than 'Noun쯤이다' (e.g. 요즘 3개에 2,000원쯤 해요).

formation: 명사 + 처럼/같이
meaning_en: like / as ... as (similarity or comparison)
meaning_zh: 像……一样；如同……（表相似或比喻）
meaning_ko: 어떤 행동이나 모습이 앞의 명사와 같거나 매우 비슷함을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: He sings like a professional singer.
Hayeong is as kind as an angel.
He's as handsome as a movie actor.
examples.chinese: 长得像电影演员一样帅。

examples.english: She's as pretty as Miss Korea.
It's crowded like Tokyo, Japan.

notes: 처럼/같이 are often used metaphorically, comparing people to animals or other things in nature: 호랑이처럼 무섭다 (scary), 토끼처럼 귀엽다 (cute), 거북이처럼 느리다 (slow), 돼지처럼 뚱뚱하다 (overweight), and 바다처럼 마음이 넓다 (generous).

formation: 명사 + 보다 (비교의 기준)
meaning_en: more ... than / -er than (marks the standard of comparison)
meaning_zh: 比……（表比较的基准）
meaning_ko: 앞의 명사를 비교의 기준으로 삼아 그보다 더함을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: Airplanes are faster than trains.
My little sister is bigger than my elder sister.
The department store is more expensive than the market.
I like spring more than summer.
examples.chinese: 比起夏天，我更喜欢春天。

examples.english: Jeju Island is warmer.

notes: 보다 is added to a noun to form 'N이/가 N보다 하다', and the order of the subject and the noun with 보다 can be reversed with no change in meaning. The adverbs 더 and 덜 are generally used together with 보다 but can be omitted.

formation: 명사 + 마다
meaning_en: every / each; once every (repetition over a set period, or every one without exception)
meaning_zh: 每……；每隔……（表反复或无一例外）
meaning_ko: 일정한 기간마다 같은 상황이나 행동이 반복되거나, 예외 없이 모든 것을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: Wesley goes to church every Sunday.
examples.chinese: 韦斯利每个星期天都去教堂。

examples.english: The train comes once every hour.
Every country has a different flag.
examples.chinese: 每个国家的国旗都不同。

examples.english: I have taekwondo lessons every Friday.
Are there computers in every classroom?

notes: 날마다, 일주일마다, 달마다, and 해마다 can also be written as 매일, 매주, 매월/매달, and 매년. For the word 집, 집집마다 is used instead of 집마다.

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -고
meaning_en: and (lists two or more actions, states, or facts; also 'and then')
meaning_zh: ……并且……（并列两个以上的动作、状态或事实；也表先后）
meaning_ko: 둘 이상의 행동이나 상태, 사실을 나열하거나 앞의 행동이 뒤의 행동보다 먼저 일어남을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: Carol is tall and slender.

examples.korean: 민우 씨는 한국 사람이고 댄 씨는 영국 사람입니다.
examples.english: Minu is Korean, and Dane is British.
examples.chinese: 民宇是韩国人，丹是英国人。

examples.korean: 어제 파티에서 티루엔 씨가 노래도 부르고 춤도 췄어요.
examples.english: At yesterday's party, Tiluen sang songs and danced.
examples.chinese: 昨天的派对上，蒂鲁恩又唱歌又跳舞。

examples.korean: 오전에는 친구를 만나고 오후에는 도서관에 갈 거예요.
examples.english: In the morning, I'll meet a friend, and in the afternoon, I'll go to the library.
examples.chinese: 上午见朋友，下午去图书馆。

examples.english: She's smart and pretty.

notes: The form 'N도 V-고 N도 V' is used when combining two or more facts about the same subject (형은 수영도 잘하고 농구도 잘해요). Note also that when -고 expresses that the first action was performed before the second, tense is expressed only in the second clause, not the first (어제 밥을 먹고 숙제를 했어요).

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -거나
meaning_en: or (a choice between two or more verbs or adjectives)
meaning_zh: 或者……；要么……要么……（在动词或形容词之间选择）
meaning_ko: 둘 이상의 동사나 형용사 중 하나를 선택함을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: In the morning, I either eat bread or drink milk.
examples.chinese: 早上要么吃面包，要么喝牛奶。

examples.korean: 주말에 음악을 듣거나 영화를 볼 거예요.
examples.english: On the weekend, I plan to listen to music or watch a movie.
examples.chinese: 周末打算听音乐或看电影。

examples.korean: 바쁘거나 가방이 무거울 때 택시를 타요.
examples.english: I take a taxi when I'm busy or my bag is too heavy.
examples.chinese: 忙的时候或包太重的时候坐出租车。

examples.english: I'll either play tennis or go swimming.
I'll take a trip or go out to eat.
examples.chinese: 打算去旅行或出去吃饭。

notes: -거나 is added to the stem of a verb or adjective; for nouns, -이나 is used instead. It is usually used once to connect two verbs or adjectives, but it can also be used to connect three or more.

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -지만 (과거: -았/었지만)
meaning_en: but (the second clause is opposite or contrary to the first)
meaning_zh: 虽然……但是……（表转折或对照）
meaning_ko: 앞 절의 내용과 반대되거나 대조되는 내용을 뒤 절에 이어 말할 때 쓰는 표현.

examples.english: Korean is difficult but interesting.
My older brother is big, but my younger brother is small.
examples.chinese: 哥哥个子大，但弟弟个子小。

examples.english: Hayeong eats a lot, but she's slim.
examples.chinese: 夏英吃得很多，但很苗条。

examples.english: It's small but clean.
He's a foreigner, but he can speak Korean well.
examples.chinese: 虽然是外国人，但韩语说得很好。

notes: -지만 is added to the stems of verbs and adjectives, and in the case of the past tense, -았/었지만 is added.

formation: 형용사 어간(받침 없음) + -ㄴ데, 형용사 어간(받침 있음) + -은데, 동사 어간·있다/없다 + -는데, 과거 + -았/었는데
meaning_en: but / though (the second clause is opposite to, in contrast with, or an unexpected result of the first)
meaning_zh: ……但是……（表转折、对照或出乎意料的结果）
meaning_ko: 앞 절의 내용과 반대되거나 대조되는 내용, 또는 예상하지 못한 결과를 뒤 절에 이어 말할 때 쓰는 표현.

examples.korean: 낮에는 차가 많은데 밤에는 차가 없어요.
examples.english: In the afternoon, there are a lot of cars, but at night, there aren't any.
examples.chinese: 白天车很多，但晚上没有车。

examples.english: I have an older brother, but not an older sister.
I can't sing, but I can dance well.
examples.chinese: 我不会唱歌，但舞跳得好。

examples.english: The prices are cheap, but it's too far away.
There are many things to do, but the salary is small.

formation: 명사 + 전에 / 동사 어간 + -기 전에
meaning_en: before (a certain period of time or some action); ago
meaning_zh: 在……之前（表时间或动作之前）
meaning_ko: 어떤 시간이나 행동보다 앞선 시점을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I came to Korea two years ago.
Please take this medicine before meals.
I do warm-up exercises before swimming.
I ate an hour ago.
Where did you live before coming to Korea?

notes: 1시 전에 오세요 means the person can come any time before 1:00, such as 12:50, 12:00, or even 11:00, while 1시간 전에 오세요 means exactly one hour before some previously stated time (e.g. 2:00 if the meeting is at 3:00). Also, 'Noun 전에' is used mainly with nouns to which 하다 can be added to make verbs; for all verbs other than 하다-verbs, only -기 전에 can be used.

formation: 명사 + 후에 / 동사 어간(모음) + -ㄴ 후에, 동사 어간(자음) + -은 후에 (어간이 'ㄹ'로 끝나면 'ㄹ'이 탈락한 뒤 -ㄴ 후에)
meaning_en: after (a certain period of time or some action); later
meaning_zh: 在……之后（表时间或动作之后）
meaning_ko: 어떤 시간이나 행동보다 뒤의 시점을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: My baby will be born in one month.
I brush my teeth after dinner.
I got a job after college graduation.
examples.chinese: 大学毕业后找到了工作。

examples.english: I'll go in one year.
It's a Korean housewarming party for someone who just moved into a new house.
examples.chinese: 这是在韩国搬家之后办的派对。

notes: 1시 후에 오세요 means the person can come any time after 1:00, such as 1:10, 2:00, or even 3:00, while 1시간 후에 오세요 means exactly one hour after some previously stated time (e.g. 4:00 if the meeting is at 3:00). -(으)ㄴ 다음에 can also be used in place of -(으)ㄴ 후에.

formation: 동사 어간 + -고 나서
meaning_en: and then / after doing (one action is completely finished, and then the next action begins)
meaning_zh: ……之后（表前一个动作完全结束后再做下一个动作）
meaning_ko: 앞의 행동을 완전히 끝낸 뒤에 뒤의 행동을 함을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I rest after finishing my work.
I sleep after watching TV.
I read the newspaper after eating breakfast.
Please give them to me after the meeting.
It's what you write after you finish reading a book.
examples.chinese: 是读完书之后写的文章。

notes: Because -고 나서 expresses temporal order, it can only be used with verbs. When the subjects of the first and second clauses are the same and the verbs are motion/position verbs such as 가다, 오다, 들어가다, 나가다, 올라가다, 내려가다, 일어나다, 앉다, 눕다, 만나다, -아/어서 is used instead of -고 나서.

formation: 동사 어간 + -아서/-어서 (하다 → 해서)
meaning_en: and then / in order to (the second action happens right after the first, the two being closely related)
meaning_zh: ……然后……（表两个紧密相关的动作先后发生）
meaning_ko: 앞의 행동이 있은 뒤에 뒤의 행동이 일어남을 나타내는 연결 어미로, 두 행동이 밀접하게 관련됨을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: (The monkey) peeled a banana and ate it.

examples.korean: 네 시간 동안 공원에 앉아서 이야기했어요.
examples.english: (We) sat in a park for four hours and talked.
examples.chinese: 在公园坐了四个小时聊天。

examples.english: I bought a necklace for my girlfriend and gave it to her.
examples.chinese: 给女朋友买了项链送给她。

examples.english: Yesterday, I met a friend to watch a movie.

examples.korean: 내일 친구를 만나서 영화를 볼 거예요.
examples.english: Tomorrow, I will meet a friend to watch a movie.

notes: The tense is expressed only in the second verb, not the first, and the subjects of both verbs must be the same. Unlike -아/어서, which links two closely related actions, -고 connects two unrelated actions that happen sequentially; with verbs for wearing clothes and accessories, -고 is used instead of -아/어서.

formation: 명사 + 때 / 동사·형용사 어간 + -(으)ㄹ 때
meaning_en: when / during (the time when an action or state occurs, or its duration)
meaning_zh: ……的时候（表动作或状态发生的时间或持续期间）
meaning_ko: 어떤 행동이나 상태가 일어나는 시간이나 그 지속되는 동안을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I work a part-time job during vacation.
This is a picture of me when I was 4 years old.

examples.korean: 시험 볼 때 옆 사람의 시험지를 보지 마세요.
examples.english: Don't look at your neighbor's answer sheet when taking the test.
examples.chinese: 考试时不要看旁边人的答题卡。

examples.korean: 몇 살 때 첫 데이트를 했어요?
examples.english: How old were you when you went on your first date?
examples.chinese: 你几岁的时候第一次约会？

notes: Check It Out!: 때 is not used together with 오전, 오후, 아침, or the days of the week (오전 때 공부를 해요 (X) → 오전에 공부를 해요 (O)). For nouns such as 저녁, 점심, and 방학, N 때 and N에 have the same meaning; for holidays such as 크리스마스 and 추석, N에 refers to the specific day(s) while N 때 refers to the approximate period around the holiday.

formation: 동사 어간 + -면서/-으면서
meaning_en: while (doing) (the actions of the first and second verbs occur simultaneously by the same subject)
meaning_zh: 一边……一边……（表同一主语同时进行两个动作）
meaning_ko: 두 동작이 같은 주체에 의해 동시에 일어남을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I eat while watching TV.

examples.korean: 우리 언니는 피아노를 치면서 노래를 해요.
examples.english: My older sister sings while she plays the piano.
examples.chinese: 我姐姐一边弹钢琴一边唱歌。

examples.english: Don't use the phone while driving. It's dangerous.
examples.chinese: 开车时不要打电话，很危险。

examples.english: I listen to music while studying.
I have a part-time job while attending school.

notes: The subjects of both clauses must be the same person; when the subjects differ, -는 동안 is used. Past and future tense endings are not added to the verb preceding -(으)면서 — it is always written in the present tense.

formation: 명사 + 중 / 동사 어간 + -는 중
meaning_en: in the process of / currently doing (the subject is in the middle of performing an action)
meaning_zh: 正在……中（表某动作正在进行）
meaning_ko: 어떤 행동이 진행 중임을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: The subway is under construction.
The president is in a meeting.
I'm on the way home.

examples.korean: 이사할 거예요. 그래서 집을 찾는 중이에요.
examples.english: I intend to move, so I'm looking for a new place to live.
examples.chinese: 我要搬家，所以正在找房子。

notes: Check It Out!: -는 중이다 and -고 있다 are used in similar ways, but -는 중이다 cannot be used with subjects representing natural phenomena (비가 오는 중이에요 (X) → 비가 오고 있어요 (O)).

formation: 동사 어간 + -자마자
meaning_en: as soon as / right after (something occurs immediately after an event or action ends)
meaning_zh: 一……就……（表前一事件刚结束就马上发生后一事件）
meaning_ko: 어떤 일이 끝난 직후에 다른 일이 바로 일어남을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I was so tired that I went to sleep as soon as I got home.
The fire truck arrived as soon as the fire started.
The students left the classroom right after class was over.
examples.chinese: 一下课学生们就出了教室。

examples.english: We'll get married as soon as we graduate from college.

notes: The subjects of the first and second clauses can be either the same or different. Tense is not expressed in the verb of the first clause, but it is in the second (집에 갔자마자 잤어요 (X) → 집에 가자마자 잤어요 (O)).

formation: 명사 + 동안 / 동사 어간 + -는 동안
meaning_en: during / while (the length of time from when an action begins until it ends)
meaning_zh: ……期间；在……的时候（表动作从开始到结束持续的时间长度）
meaning_ko: 어떤 행동이 시작해서 끝날 때까지의 시간 길이를 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: Yesterday, I studied for four hours.
Bears hibernate during winter.

examples.korean: 친구들이 점심을 먹는 동안 나는 숙제를 했어요.
examples.english: I did my homework while my friends were eating lunch.
examples.chinese: 朋友们吃午饭的时候我做了作业。

examples.korean: (내가) 한국에서 사는 동안 (나는) 좋은 친구들을 많이 만났어요.
examples.english: While I lived in Korea, I made a lot of good friends.
examples.chinese: 我在韩国生活期间交了很多好朋友。

notes: What's the Difference?: -(으)면서 is used when one person performs two or more actions simultaneously and requires the same subject in both clauses, whereas -는 동안(에) can be used even when the subjects of the first and second clauses are different.

formation: 동사 어간 + -ㄴ 지/-은 지
meaning_en: since (how much time has passed since a situation or action occurred)
meaning_zh: ……以来（表某动作或情况发生后到现在过了多久）
meaning_ko: 어떤 일이 일어난 후 지금까지 얼마의 시간이 지났음을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: It's been two years since I came to Korea.

examples.korean: 담배 끊은 지 한 달 되었어요.
examples.english: It's been one month since I stopped smoking.
It's been over five hours since you started playing computer games.
examples.chinese: 你玩电脑游戏已经超过五个小时了。

examples.english: It's been six months since I began studying Korean.
examples.chinese: 我学韩语已经六个月了。

examples.english: We've been dating for over three years.

formation: 동사 어간 + -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다
meaning_en: can / cannot (expressing ability or possibility)
meaning_zh: 能/不能……；可以/不可以……（表能力或可能性）
meaning_ko: 어떤 일을 할 수 있는 능력이나 가능성을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: We can see this movie.
We can't see that movie.
I can speak Korean.
I can read Chinese characters.
I can't read Chinese characters.

notes: Check It Out!: Adding the particle -가 to -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 to form -(으)ㄹ 수가 있다/없다 makes the phrase more emphatic than -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 alone.

formation: 동사 어간 + -(으)ㄹ 줄 알다/모르다
meaning_en: know how to / don't know how to (knowing how, or having the ability, to do something)
meaning_zh: 会/不会……（表知道做某事的方法或有此能力）
meaning_ko: 어떤 일을 하는 방법을 알고 있거나 그 능력이 있음을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I know how to make strawberry jam.
I know how to send pictures by mobile phone.
I know how to cook a tasty doenjang stew.

examples.korean: 저는 잡채하고 스파게티를 만들 줄 알아요.
examples.english: I know how to make Korean japchae and spaghetti.
examples.chinese: 我会做杂菜和意大利面。

notes: What's the Difference?: -(으)ㄹ 줄 알다/모르다 expresses whether one knows how or has the skill to do something, whereas -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 is used not only to express ability but also whether a situation permits something to be done.

formation: 동사 어간 + -세요/-으세요 (일부 동사는 특수 형태)
meaning_en: please do (a polite request, command, or instruction to the listener)
meaning_zh: 请……（礼貌地请求、指示或命令对方做某事）
meaning_ko: 듣는 사람에게 정중하게 어떤 행동을 하도록 요청하거나 명령할 때 쓰는 표현.

examples.english: Please sit here.
Please look at page 15 in the book.
Please go straight up this road.
Please write down your name and phone number here.
examples.chinese: 请在这里写下姓名和电话号码。

examples.english: Everyone, please be quiet!

notes: When -(으)세요 is used in the imperative sense, it can only be used with verbs, not 이다 or adjectives (의사이세요 (X) → 의사가 되세요 (O); 기쁘세요 (X) → 기뻐하세요 (O)). However, some adjectives ending in 하다 used idiomatically can be used with -으세요, e.g. 건강하세요, 행복하세요.

formation: 동사 어간 + -지 마세요
meaning_en: please don't do (a negative request, persuasion, or command)
meaning_zh: 请不要……（表否定的请求、劝告或命令）
meaning_ko: 듣는 사람에게 어떤 행동을 하지 말라고 요청하거나 명령할 때 쓰는 표현.

examples.english: Please don't drink alcohol.
Please don't use the phone.
Please don't sleep during class.
There's a lot of traffic, so don't take the bus.
examples.chinese: 路上堵车，请不要坐公交车。

examples.english: Please don't see this movie. It's boring.
examples.chinese: 请不要看这部电影，没意思。

notes: -지 마세요 can only be used with verbs, not 이다 or adjectives (슬프지 마세요 (X) → 슬퍼하세요 (O)).
unit: Demands and Obligations, Permission and Prohibition

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -아야/-어야 되다/하다 (하다 → 해야 되다/하다)
meaning_en: must / have to (expressing obligation, necessity, or the necessity of a certain condition)
meaning_zh: 必须……；得……（表义务、必要或某种情况的必要性）
meaning_ko: 어떤 일을 해야 할 의무나 필요가 있음을 나타내는 표현.

examples.korean: 내일 시험이 있어요. 그래서 공부해야 돼요.
examples.english: I have an exam tomorrow. So I must study.
examples.chinese: 明天有考试，所以必须学习。

examples.korean: 여자 친구 생일이라서 선물을 사야 돼요.
examples.english: It's my girlfriend's birthday, so I have to buy her a present.
examples.chinese: 因为女朋友过生日，所以要买礼物。

examples.english: You have to pay before you eat.
I have to visit home.
You have to reserve your ticket in advance.

notes: Check It Out!: -아/어야 되다/하다 has two negative forms — -지 않아도 되다 (don't need to, don't have to) and -(으)면 안 되다 (shouldn't, not allowed to).
unit: Demands and Obligations, Permission and Prohibition

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -아도/-어도 되다 (하다 → 해도 되다)
meaning_en: may / be allowed to (expressing permission or approval for a behavior)
meaning_zh: 可以……；……也行（表许可或同意）
meaning_ko: 어떤 행동을 해도 괜찮음을 나타내는 허락이나 승인의 표현.

examples.english: May I take a picture?
May I sit here?
May I use that pen?
Do you mind if I open the window?
May I turn on the radio?

notes: In place of -아/어도 되다, -아/어도 괜찮다 and -아/어도 좋다 can also be used.
unit: Demands and Obligations, Permission and Prohibition

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -면/-으면 안 되다
meaning_en: may not / not allowed to (expressing prohibition or limitation of a particular action)
meaning_zh: 不可以……；不能……（表禁止或限制）
meaning_ko: 어떤 행동을 하면 안 된다는 금지나 제한을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: Smoking indoors is not allowed.
Using the phone while driving is not allowed.
You may not cross the street now.

examples.korean: 수업 시간에는 영어로 말하면 안 돼요.
examples.english: During class, you may not speak in English.
examples.chinese: 上课时间不可以说英语。

examples.english: You're not allowed to talk in the library.

notes: Check It Out!: -으면 안 되다 can be used in the double negative form -지 않으면 안 되다 to emphasize that a particular behavior must be performed (사지 않으면 안 돼요 = 사야 돼요).
unit: Demands and Obligations, Permission and Prohibition

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -지 않아도 되다 (= 안 -아/어도 되다)
meaning_en: don't have to / need not (expressing that a behavior or state is not necessary)
meaning_zh: 不用……；不必……（表没有必要做某事）
meaning_ko: 어떤 행동을 하지 않아도 괜찮음을 나타내는 표현으로, '-아/어야 되다/하다'의 부정형.

examples.korean: 유치원생은 버스 요금을 내지 않아도 돼요.
examples.english: Preschool students don't have to pay the bus fare.
examples.chinese: 幼儿园学生不用付公交车费。

examples.korean: 평일이니까 영화표를 미리 사지 않아도 돼요.
examples.english: Because it's a weekday, we don't have to buy tickets in advance.
examples.chinese: 因为是平日，不用提前买电影票。

examples.english: On Fridays, we don't have to wear suits.
If you're busy, you don't have to go.
You don't need to diet.

formation: 동사 어간 + -고 싶다
meaning_en: want to (expressing the speaker's wish or hope)
meaning_zh: 想……；想要……（表说话人的愿望或希望）
meaning_ko: 말하는 사람의 바람이나 희망을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I want to speak Korean well.
I want to see my family.
I want to eat strawberries.
I want to drink some coffee.
I'd like some nice looking gloves.

notes: Check It Out!: When the subject is in the third person, -고 싶어하다 is used (에릭 씨는 자동차를 사고 싶어요 (X) → 사고 싶어해요 (O)). -고 싶다 cannot be added directly to adjectives, but if -아/어지다 is added first to make it a verb, it can be used (날씬하고 싶어요 (X) → 날씬해지고 싶어요 (O)). -고 싶다 can be combined with the particles -을/를 and -이/가.

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -았/었으면 좋겠다 (하다 → 했으면 좋겠다)
meaning_en: I wish / I hope (expressing a wish or hope about something not yet realized)
meaning_zh: 要是……就好了；希望……（表对尚未实现之事的愿望或希望）
meaning_ko: 아직 실현되지 않은 일에 대한 바람이나 희망을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I wish I had a car.
I wish I had a lot of money.
I hope it snows on Christmas.
I'd like to get married before I'm 30.
I wish I could have some time off.

notes: Check It Out!: -(으)면 좋겠다 can be used in the same sense as -았/었으면 좋겠다, but because -았/었으면 좋겠다 supposes the realization of an as yet unrealized state, it more strongly emphasizes the wish.

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -아/어서 (어간의 모음이 ㅏ/ㅗ이면 -아서, 그 외에는 -어서, 하다→해서, 이다→이어서/이라서)
meaning_en: because / so / on account of (the first clause is the reason or cause of the second)
meaning_zh: 因为……；所以……（表原因或理由）
meaning_ko: 앞 절의 내용이 뒤 절의 이유나 원인이 됨을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: Nice to meet you.
I was in such a good mood that I danced.
examples.chinese: 因为心情好，所以跳舞了。

examples.english: I'm sorry for arriving late.
This week I'm busy, so I don't have time.
examples.chinese: 这周很忙，所以没有时间。

examples.english: Those clothes are so small that I can't wear them.
examples.chinese: 那件衣服太小了，穿不了。

notes: -아/어서 cannot be used in imperative or propositive sentences (use -(으)니까 instead). Tense markers such as -았/었- and -겠- cannot come before -아/어서.

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -(으)니까 (어간이 모음으로 끝나면 -니까, 자음으로 끝나면 -으니까)
meaning_en: because / so (expressing a reason or cause)
meaning_zh: 因为……；所以……（表原因或理由）
meaning_ko: 앞 절이 뒤 절의 이유나 원인이 됨을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: The roads are full of traffic, so let's take the subway.
examples.chinese: 路上堵车，所以坐地铁吧。

examples.english: It's cold, so please close the window.
I took a shower, so now I feel good.
examples.chinese: 洗了个澡，所以心情很好。

examples.korean: 이번 주는 바쁘니까 다음 주에 합시다.
examples.english: This week I'm busy, so let's do it next week.
examples.chinese: 这周很忙，所以下周做吧。

examples.english: Girls like flowers, so give her some flowers.
examples.chinese: 女孩子喜欢花，所以送花吧。

notes: Unlike -아/어서, -(으)니까 can be used with imperative and propositive sentences, and tense markers such as -았/었- and -겠- can precede it.

formation: 명사 + 때문에 / 동사·형용사 어간 + -기 때문에
meaning_en: because of (N) / because (A/V) — reason or cause
meaning_zh: 因为……（名词后用 때문에，动词/形容词后用 -기 때문에）
meaning_ko: 앞 절이 뒤 절 상황의 이유나 원인임을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: The road is slippery because of the snow.
I'm tired because of the children.
I can't speak Korean well because I'm a foreigner.
examples.chinese: 因为我是外国人，所以韩语说得不好。

examples.english: There was a lot of traffic due to the rain.
examples.chinese: 因为下雨，车堵得很厉害。

examples.korean: 토요일은 친구 생일이기 때문에 만날 수 없어요.
examples.english: Saturday is my friend's birthday, so I won't be able to meet you.
examples.chinese: 周六是我朋友的生日，所以见不了面。

notes: -기 때문에 cannot be used in imperative or propositive sentences (use -(으)니까 instead).

formation: 동사 어간 + -아/어 주세요 / -아/어 주시겠어요? (어간의 모음이 ㅏ/ㅗ이면 -아 주세요, 그 외에는 -어 주세요, 하다→해 주세요; 높임 대상에는 -아/어 드리세요)
meaning_en: please do (something for me/someone); would you please do ... — making a request
meaning_zh: 请……（为某人做某事）
meaning_ko: 다른 사람에게 어떤 행동을 해 줄 것을 요청하는 표현.

examples.english: Please close the door.
Would you please take our picture?
examples.chinese: 能请您帮我们拍张照吗？

examples.english: Please show her to a seat.
Excuse me, could you please help me out?

examples.korean: 왕단 씨, 이 문법 좀 가르쳐 주세요.
examples.english: Wang Dan, please teach me this grammar.
examples.chinese: 王丹，请教我一下这个语法。

notes: -아/어 주다/드리다 is used when the speaker or the subject of the sentence performs an action that assists the listener or another person. When the assistance has already been completed, -아/어 줬어요 or -아/어 드렸어요 is used.

formation: 동사 어간 + -아/어 줄게요 / -아/어 줄까요? (어간의 모음이 ㅏ/ㅗ이면 -아 줄게요, 그 외에는 -어 줄게요, 하다→해 줄게요; 높임 대상에는 -아/어 드릴게요/드릴까요?)
meaning_en: shall I / let me / I'll do (something for you) — offering help
meaning_zh: 我（来）给你……吧；要我帮你……吗？
meaning_ko: 다른 사람을 돕기 위해 어떤 행동을 하겠다는 뜻을 나타내는 표현.

examples.korean: 우산이 두 개 있는데 빌려 줄까요?
examples.english: I have two umbrellas, so shall I lend you one?
examples.chinese: 我有两把伞，要借给你一把吗？

examples.english: Let me help you with that.
Teacher, shall I help you out?
Okay, I'll clear it off right away.
examples.chinese: 好的，客人，我马上给您收拾。

examples.english: Sure, I'll turn it on.

formation: 동사 어간 + -아/어 보다 (어간의 모음이 ㅏ/ㅗ이면 -아 보다, 그 외에는 -어 보다, 하다→해 보다)
meaning_en: to try doing (something); to have the experience of doing
meaning_zh: 尝试做……；（曾经）做过……
meaning_ko: 어떤 행동을 시도하거나 경험해 봄을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: Have you tried Korean ribs?
Please try it on.
I want to visit Jeju Island.
May I try on these shoes?
examples.chinese: 我可以试穿一下这双鞋吗？

examples.english: Yes, please try them on.

notes: When -아/어 보다 is used to express the experiencing of something, it is not used together with the verb 보다 (e.g., 한국 영화를 봐 봤어요 (X) → 한국 영화를 본 적이 있어요 (O)).
unit: Unit 11: Trying New Things and Experiences

formation: 동사 어간 + -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다/없다 (어간이 모음으로 끝나면 -ㄴ 적이 있다/없다, 자음으로 끝나면 -은 적이 있다/없다)
meaning_en: to have / have not (ever) done; expressing past experience
meaning_zh: （曾经）做过……／（从未）做过……（表过去经历）
meaning_ko: 과거에 어떤 일을 경험했거나 경험하지 않았음을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I've seen an Indian movie.
I've never been late to work.
Have you ever been to Italy?

examples.korean: 와, 난 지금까지 한 번도 연예인을 만난 적이 없어요.
examples.english: Wow, I've never met a celebrity.
examples.chinese: 哇，我到现在一次都没见过艺人。

examples.english: No, I've never been able to bargain.

notes: -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다 is not used when describing things that are often repeated or are everyday occurrences.
unit: Unit 11: Trying New Things and Experiences

formation: 동사 어간 + -(으)ㄹ까요? (어간이 모음이나 ㄹ로 끝나면 -ㄹ까요?, 자음으로 끝나면 -을까요?)
meaning_en: shall we ...? (suggesting doing something together with the listener)
meaning_zh: 我们……好吗？（表提议一起做某事）
meaning_ko: 함께 무엇을 하자고 제안하거나 상대방의 의견을 물을 때 쓰는 표현.

examples.english: Shall we play some basketball?
Why don't we rest over here?
Which movie shall we see?
Shall we go sing karaoke over the weekend?
examples.chinese: 周末一起去练歌房好吗？

examples.korean: 퇴근 후에 술 한 잔 할까요?
examples.english: Would you like to go for a drink after work?
examples.chinese: 下班后去喝一杯怎么样？

unit: Unit 12: Asking Opinions and Making Suggestions

formation: 동사 어간 + -(으)ㅂ시다 (어간이 모음으로 끝나면 -ㅂ시다, 자음으로 끝나면 -읍시다); 부정은 -지 맙시다/-지 마요
meaning_en: let's ... (suggesting or proposing to do something together)
meaning_zh: 让我们……吧（表提议或劝诱）
meaning_ko: 함께 무엇을 하자고 제안하거나 권유할 때 쓰는 표현.

examples.english: Let's eat Korean food.
Let's not take the bus. Let's take the subway.
examples.chinese: 别坐公交车，我们坐地铁吧。

examples.english: Let's not see a movie.
Let's leave in 10 minutes.

examples.korean: 월요일에 시험이 있으니까 클럽에 가지 맙시다. 같이 공부합시다.
examples.english: We have a test on Monday, so let's not go to a club. Let's study together.
examples.chinese: 周一有考试，所以我们别去夜店了。一起学习吧。

notes: -(으)ㅂ시다 can be used in formal situations when suggesting or urging a group of people to do something, or when the listener is younger or of lower status than the speaker. It cannot be used toward someone older or of higher status than the speaker; in such cases 같이 -(으)세요 is appropriate.
unit: Unit 12: Asking Opinions and Making Suggestions

formation: 동사 어간 + -(으)시겠어요? (어간이 모음으로 끝나면 -시겠어요?, 자음으로 끝나면 -으시겠어요?)
meaning_en: would you (like to) ...? (polite suggestion or asking about the listener's intention)
meaning_zh: 您要……吗？／您愿意……吗？（礼貌地提议或询问意向）
meaning_ko: 상대방에게 공손하게 제안하거나 그 의향을 물을 때 쓰는 표현.

examples.english: Would you like a donut?
Would you like to reserve a room?
Would you like sugar in your coffee?
What time will you come tomorrow?
Would you mind calling me in 30 minutes?
examples.chinese: 能请您30分钟后再打给我吗？

unit: Unit 12: Asking Opinions and Making Suggestions

formation: 동사 어간 + -(으)ㄹ래요? (어간이 모음이나 ㄹ로 끝나면 -ㄹ래요?, 자음으로 끝나면 -을래요?)
meaning_en: do you want to ...? / how about ...? (asking the listener's preference or intention)
meaning_zh: 你想……吗？／……怎么样？（询问对方意向或偏好）
meaning_ko: 상대방의 의향이나 취향을 묻거나 부드럽게 요청할 때 쓰는 표현.

examples.english: Do you want to go hiking?
Would you like to have a cup of coffee?
Would you like to go ride a boat on the Han River?
I'll have beef rib soup.
In that case, how about going to Seoul Tower this evening?
examples.chinese: 那今晚一起去首尔塔怎么样？

unit: Unit 12: Asking Opinions and Making Suggestions

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -겠어요 (부정: -지 않겠어요 / 안 -겠어요)
meaning_en: I will / I'm going to (the speaker's intention or will); also 'should/will' for something about to happen
meaning_zh: 我要……；我会……（表说话人的意志）；也表即将发生的事
meaning_ko: 화자의 의지나 의도를 나타내거나, 곧 일어날 일을 추측할 때 쓰는 표현.

examples.english: This year I'm going to stop smoking.
I'll go on the business trip.
We will soon arrive at Incheon Airport.
examples.chinese: 我们马上就要到达仁川机场了。

examples.english: I plan to exercise every morning.
I will arrive early starting tomorrow.

notes: When -겠어요 is used to express intention or will, the subject cannot be in the third person. -겠- is also used idiomatically in expressions such as 처음 뵙겠습니다 (Nice to meet you), 잘 먹겠습니다 (Thank you for the food), and 학교 다녀오겠습니다 (I'm off to school), and when the speaker wants to be less assertive and more gentle and polite.

formation: 동사 어간 + -(으)ㄹ게요 (어간이 모음이나 ㄹ로 끝나면 -ㄹ게요, 자음으로 끝나면 -을게요)
meaning_en: I will (do) — expressing the speaker's decision, intention, or a promise to the listener
meaning_zh: 我会……的（表说话人的决心、意志或对对方的承诺）
meaning_ko: 화자가 앞으로 할 일에 대한 결정이나 의지를 상대방에게 약속하듯 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I'll answer the phone.
Sorry, I have work to do, so I'll be leaving now.
I'll call you in the evening.
I'll definitely bring it tomorrow.

examples.korean: 네, 알아요. 제가 종이에 써 드릴게요.
examples.english: Yes, I do. I'll write it down (on paper) for you.
examples.chinese: 嗯，知道。我给您写在纸上。

notes: This expression can be used only with verbs that express the will of the subject (it cannot be used with adjectives), only with first-person subjects, and cannot be used in questions.

formation: 동사 어간 + -(으)ㄹ래요 (어간이 모음이나 ㄹ로 끝나면 -ㄹ래요, 자음으로 끝나면 -을래요)
meaning_en: I will / I'm going to (expressing the speaker's will or intention)
meaning_zh: 我要……；我打算……（表说话人的意志或打算）
meaning_ko: 화자가 무엇을 하겠다는 의지나 의향을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I'm so full. I'm not going to eat any more.
I'll have some coffee.
This vacation, I'm going on a trip.
I'd like some coffee.

examples.korean: 네, 안 갈래요. 피곤해서 집에서 쉴래요.
examples.english: No, I'm not going. I'm tired, so I plan on resting at home.
examples.chinese: 嗯，不去了。我累了，想在家休息。

notes: This expression can be used only with verbs, and only with first-person subjects.

formation: 동사 어간 + -(으)니까 (어간이 모음으로 끝나면 -니까, 자음으로 끝나면 -으니까)
meaning_en: when / only to discover — expressing the discovery of a fact as a result of performing an action
meaning_zh: （做了某事）结果发现／才知道……
meaning_ko: 앞 절의 행동을 한 결과 뒤 절의 사실을 발견하게 됨을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I arrived home to discover the smell of something tasty.
examples.chinese: 一进家门就闻到香喷喷的味道。

examples.english: When I woke up in the morning, the gift had already arrived.
examples.chinese: 早上起来一看，礼物已经到了。

examples.english: When I arrived home, it was midnight.
examples.chinese: 回到家一看，已经是晚上12点了。

examples.english: Yes, but only to find he did not answer.
examples.chinese: 嗯，可是打过去发现他不接。

examples.korean: 만 원이요. 어제 백화점에 가니까 세일을 하고 있었어요.
examples.english: 10,000 won. When I went to the department store yesterday, they were having a sale.
examples.chinese: 一万韩元。昨天去百货商店一看，正在打折。

notes: When -(으)니까 expresses the result of an action (discovery), -았/었- and -겠- cannot precede it.

formation: 동사 어간 + -(으)러 가다/오다 (어간이 모음이나 ㄹ로 끝나면 -러 가다/오다, 자음으로 끝나면 -으러 가다/오다)
meaning_en: to go / come in order to (do something)
meaning_zh: 去／来（做某事）（表目的）
meaning_ko: 어떤 행동을 하기 위해 장소로 가거나 옴을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: We're going to Dongdaemun Market to buy clothes.
examples.chinese: 我们去东大门市场买衣服。

examples.english: I came to Korea to see my Korean fans.
examples.chinese: 我为了见韩国粉丝来到了韩国。

examples.english: I'm going to the bank to withdraw some money.
Please come to visit over the weekend.
I'm attending an academy to learn Korean dance.

notes: Only movement verbs such as 가다, 오다, and 다니다 can be used after -(으)러. Other movement verbs such as 가다, 오다, 올라가다, 내려가다, 들어가다, 나가다, 여행하다, and 이사하다 cannot be used before -(으)러.

formation: 동사 어간 + -(으)려고 (어간이 모음으로 끝나면 -려고, 자음으로 끝나면 -으려고)
meaning_en: in order to / so that (expresses the speaker's intention or plan)
meaning_zh: 为了……；打算……（表说话人的意图或计划）
meaning_ko: 말하는 사람의 의도나 계획을 나타내는 표현으로, 뒤 절의 내용을 이루기 위해 앞 절의 행동을 함을 나타낸다.

examples.korean: 살을 빼려고 매일 세 시간씩 운동을 해요.
examples.english: I exercise three hours a day to try to lose weight.
examples.chinese: 为了减肥，我每天运动三个小时。

examples.english: I bought a present to give to my wife.
examples.chinese: 我买了一份礼物，打算送给妻子。

examples.english: I drank five cups of coffee so that I wouldn't go to sleep.
examples.chinese: 为了不睡着，我喝了整整五杯咖啡。

examples.korean: 네, 컴퓨터를 배우려고 하원에 다니고 있어요.
examples.english: Yes, I go to an academy to learn how to use computers.
examples.chinese: 是的，我为了学电脑而去学院上课。

examples.english: I called so that I could hear your voice.
examples.chinese: 我打电话是为了听你的声音。

notes: Compared with -(으)러: -(으)러 is used only with movement verbs such as 가다, 오다, 다니다, 올라가다 and 나가다, whereas -(으)려고 can be used with all verbs. -(으)러 can follow present, past and future tense verbs, but -(으)려고 sounds awkward with a future tense verb. -(으)러 can combine with -(으)ㅂ시다 and -(으)세요, while -(으)려고 cannot.

formation: 동사 어간 + -(으)려고 하다 (어간이 모음으로 끝나면 -려고 하다, 자음으로 끝나면 -으려고 하다)
meaning_en: plan to / intend to (the subject's intention or plan not yet acted upon)
meaning_zh: 打算……；计划……（表主语的意图或尚未实行的计划）
meaning_ko: 주어의 의도나 아직 행동으로 옮기지 않은 계획을 나타내는 표현이다.

examples.english: I plan to travel during the summer vacation.

examples.korean: 결혼하면 아이를 두 명 낳으려고 해요.
examples.english: I intend to have two children once I'm married.
examples.chinese: 我打算结婚后生两个孩子。

examples.korean: 방학 동안 운전을 배우려고 했어요. 그런데 팔을 다쳐서 못 배웠어요.
examples.english: I had planned on learning how to drive during the vacation. But I injured my arm and wasn't able to.
examples.chinese: 我本来打算假期学开车，但胳膊受了伤，没能学成。

examples.english: I plan to buy a new car.
I plan on getting a job at a company.

notes: -(으)려고 했다 is the past tense form of -(으)려고 하다; it is used when the intended action or plan did not materialize as expected.

formation: 명사 + 을/를 위해(서); 동사 어간 + -기 위해(서)
meaning_en: for the sake of / in order to (do something for the sake of or to accomplish something)
meaning_zh: 为了……（表为了某事或为达成某目的而行动）
meaning_ko: 어떤 일을 위해서나 어떤 것을 이루기 위해서 행동함을 나타내는 표현이다.

examples.korean: 건강을 위해서 매일 비타민을 먹고 있습니다.
examples.english: I take vitamins daily for my health.
examples.chinese: 为了健康，我每天吃维生素。

examples.english: Soldiers are people who work for their country.
examples.chinese: 军人是为国家工作的人。

examples.korean: 훌륭한 스케이트 선수가 되기 위해 열심히 연습을 합니다.
examples.english: I practice hard to become a great skater.
examples.chinese: 为了成为优秀的滑冰选手，我努力练习。

examples.korean: 저는 가족을 위해서 매일 기도하고 있어요.
examples.english: I pray for my family every day.

examples.korean: 이 집을 사기 위해서 우리 부부가 열심히 돈을 모았어요.
examples.english: We both worked hard to save money to buy this home.
examples.chinese: 为了买这套房子，我们夫妻俩努力攒钱。

notes: -기 위해서 cannot be added directly to adjectives; however, if -아/어지다 has been added to an adjective, making it a verb, then it can be used with -기 위해서 (e.g. 건강해지기 위해서 운동을 합니다, not 건강하기 위해서). Compared with -(으)려고, -기 위해서 can be used with -아/어야 해요, -(으)ㅂ시다, -(으)세요 and -(으)ㄹ까요?, while -(으)려고 cannot.

formation: 동사 어간 + -기로 하다
meaning_en: decide to / make a promise to (do something)
meaning_zh: 决定……；约定……（表与他人约定或自己下决心）
meaning_ko: 다른 사람과 약속을 하거나 스스로 결심한 내용을 나타내는 표현이다.

examples.korean: 건강 때문에 올해부터 담배를 끊기로 했어요.
examples.english: I made the decision to stop smoking for my health starting this year.
examples.chinese: 因为健康原因，我决定从今年开始戒烟。

examples.english: I decided to go hiking with my friend over the weekend.
examples.chinese: 我决定周末和朋友一起去爬山。

examples.english: We've decided to get married three years from now.

examples.korean: 이번 주말에 캐럴 씨와 데이트하기로 했어요.
examples.english: Carol and I have decided to go on a date this weekend.
examples.chinese: 我和卡萝尔决定这个周末去约会。

examples.english: Budi decided to bring one.

notes: While -기로 하다 is mainly used in its past tense forms of -기로 했어요/했습니다, it is sometimes used in its present tense form of -기로 해요. In such cases, it refers to the speaker and listener making a promise to do something.

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -(으)면 (어간이 모음으로 끝나면 -면, 자음으로 끝나면 -으면)
meaning_en: if / when / once (expresses a condition or a supposition)
meaning_zh: 如果……；（如果）……的话（表条件或假设）
meaning_ko: 어떤 사실이나 반복되는 상황의 조건을 나타내거나 아직 실현되지 않은 상황을 가정할 때 쓰는 표현이다.

examples.english: If you spend too much time on the computer, your eyes hurt.
I dance when I'm in a good mood.
examples.chinese: 我心情好的时候就跳舞。

examples.korean: 돈을 많이 벌면 집을 살 거예요.
examples.english: If I make a lot of money, I'm going to buy a house.
examples.chinese: 如果赚很多钱，我就买房子。

examples.korean: 날씨가 좋으면 등산을 해요. 그렇지만 비나 눈이 오면 집에서 텔레비전을 봐요.
examples.english: If the weather's nice, I go hiking. But if it rains or snows, then I watch TV at home.
examples.chinese: 天气好的话就去爬山，但下雨或下雪的话就在家看电视。

examples.english: Please stay in touch when you're back home.
examples.chinese: 回到家乡后请跟我联系。

notes: Information about something that happened in the past cannot come before -(으)면; when an action occurs only once, -(으)ㄹ 때 is used instead (e.g. 어제 영화를 볼 때 울었어요, not 보면). Also, when the subjects of the first and second clauses are different, the particle following the subject of the first clause changes from 은/는 to 이/가.

formation: 동사 어간 + -(으)려면 (어간이 모음으로 끝나면 -려면, 자음으로 끝나면 -으려면)
meaning_en: if you want to / if your intention is to
meaning_zh: 如果想……的话（表为达成某意图所需的条件）
meaning_ko: 앞 절에서 어떤 계획이나 의도를 말하고, 그 계획을 이루기 위해 필요한 조건을 뒤 절에서 제시하는 표현이다.

examples.english: If you want to play basketball well, you have to be able to jump high.
examples.chinese: 要想篮球打得好，就得跳得高。

examples.english: If you're trying to get to Dongdaemun, then please take subway line 4.
examples.chinese: 如果要去东大门，请坐地铁4号线。

examples.korean: 이 선생님을 만나려면 월요일에 학교로 가세요.
examples.english: If you want to meet with teacher Lee, then come to school on Monday.
examples.chinese: 如果想见李老师，请周一去学校。

examples.english: If you want to speak Korean well, then only speak Korean every day.
examples.chinese: 要想韩语说得好，就每天只用韩语对话。

examples.english: If you don't want to lose your pen, then write your name on it.
examples.chinese: 如果不想弄丢笔，就在上面写上名字。

notes: -(으)려면 is the shortened form of -(으)려고 하면. It is common for the following forms to be used in the second clause: -아/어야 해요/돼요, -(으)면 돼요, -(으)세요, 이/가 필요해요 and -는 게 좋아요.

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -아/어도 (어간 끝 모음이 ㅏ/ㅗ이면 -아도, 그 외에는 -어도, 하다이면 -해도)
meaning_en: even if / regardless of whether
meaning_zh: 即使……也……；不管……都……
meaning_ko: 앞 절의 행동이나 상태와 상관없이 뒤 절의 상황이 일어남을 나타내는 표현이다.

examples.english: Grandma can't hear you even if you speak loudly.
examples.chinese: 就算大声说，奶奶也听不见。

examples.korean: 이 옷이 마음에 들어요. 비싸도 사고 싶어요.
examples.english: I like these clothes. I want to buy them even if they are expensive.
examples.chinese: 我喜欢这件衣服。就算贵也想买。

examples.english: Even if I listen to the news, I can't understand it.
examples.chinese: 就算听新闻，我也听不懂。

examples.english: It's 2:50 right now. We won't make it by 3:00 even if we take a taxi.
examples.chinese: 现在2点50分。就算打车，3点前也到不了。

examples.korean: 바빠도 아침 식사를 꼭 해야 해요.
examples.english: You have to eat breakfast even if you're busy.
examples.chinese: 就算忙，也一定要吃早饭。

notes: The meaning of -아/어도 can be emphasized by using 아무리 in front of the verb, giving the expression the meaning of 'no matter how (much)'.

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -(으)ㄹ 거예요 (어간이 모음으로 끝나면 -ㄹ 거예요, 자음으로 끝나면 -을 거예요; 과거 추측은 -았/었을 거예요)
meaning_en: think / will (the speaker's supposition based on personal experience or on something seen or heard)
meaning_zh: （我）想会……；大概会……（表有依据的推测）
meaning_ko: 개인적인 경험이나 보고 들은 것을 근거로 한 추측을 나타내는 표현이다.

examples.english: You'll be hot if you wear that.
examples.chinese: 穿那件衣服的话会很热。

examples.korean: 하영 씨에게는 보라색 티셔츠가 잘 어울릴 거예요.
examples.english: I think Hayeong would look good in a violet T-shirt.
examples.chinese: 我觉得紫色T恤会很适合夏英。

examples.english: I think Dane has already left work because it's 7:00.
examples.chinese: 现在7点了，丹应该已经下班了。

examples.korean: 네, 그렇지만 자주 안 와서 지하철이 더 편할 거예요.
examples.english: Yes, there is, but it doesn't come very often, so the subway may be more convenient.
examples.chinese: 有，但不常来，所以坐地铁可能更方便。

examples.korean: 매일 음악을 들으면서 다니니까 좋아할 거예요.
examples.english: He listens to music every day on the way to school, so I think he'd like it.
examples.chinese: 他每天上学路上都听音乐，所以应该会喜欢。

notes: When used to indicate supposition, -(으)ㄹ 거예요 cannot be used in questions; for questions -(으)ㄹ까요? is used.

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -(으)ㄹ까요? (어간이 모음으로 끝나면 -ㄹ까요?, 자음으로 끝나면 -을까요?; 과거 추측은 -았/었을까요?)
meaning_en: I wonder if... / do you think...? (supposition in question form)
meaning_zh: 会……吗？；（你）觉得会……吗？（表推测的疑问句）
meaning_ko: 아직 일어나지 않은 일에 대한 추측을 의문문으로 나타내는 표현이다.

examples.english: Do you think the weather will be hot this weekend?
Will Carol show up today?
Do you think Dan has read this book?
Do you think flowers are expensive these days?
Do you think there will be much traffic if we go now?
examples.chinese: 现在去的话路上会堵吗？

notes: In response, -(으)ㄹ 거예요 and (으)ㄴ/는 것 같아요 are often used.

formation: 형용사 현재 -(으)ㄴ 것 같다; 동사 현재 -는 것 같다; 동사 과거 -(으)ㄴ 것 같다; 동사 미래 -(으)ㄹ 것 같다
meaning_en: it looks / sounds / seems like (supposition; also used to state one's opinion politely and indirectly)
meaning_zh: 好像……；似乎……（表推测，也用于委婉表达个人看法）
meaning_ko: 어떤 일이 일어난 것 같거나 앞으로 일어날 것이라고 추측할 때, 또는 자신의 생각을 완곡하게 말할 때 쓰는 표현이다.

examples.english: It looks like it rained yesterday.
It looks like it's raining right now.
It looks like it's going to rain.
It seems a little salty.
It seems like the week is just flying by.

examples.korean: 그 식당 주인이 친절한 것 같아요.
examples.english: That restaurant owner seems nice.
examples.chinese: 那家餐厅的老板好像很亲切。

notes: -(으)ㄴ 것 같다 is a more direct expression and is used when the speaker has a clear and definite basis for the supposition. -(으)ㄹ 것 같다, on the other hand, is more indirect and is therefore used when making a vague supposition.

formation: 형용사 현재 -(으)ㄴ N; 동사 현재 -는 N; 동사 과거 -(으)ㄴ N; 동사 미래 -(으)ㄹ N (부정형: 형용사 -지 않은 N, 동사 -지 않는 N)
meaning_en: noun-modifying form 'that / who' (allows verbs and adjectives to modify nouns)
meaning_zh: ……的（定语形，使动词、形容词修饰名词）
meaning_ko: 동사나 형용사가 명사를 수식할 수 있게 하는 관형사형 표현이다.

examples.english: I want to buy a pretty purse.
Who is that person (who is) sleeping on the sofa?
examples.chinese: 在沙发上睡觉的人是谁？

examples.korean: 오늘 저녁에 먹을 한국 음식이 뭐예요?
examples.english: What's the Korean dish (that) we'll have for dinner today?
examples.chinese: 今晚要吃的韩国菜是什么？

examples.english: I like funny movies.
Who is the person (who is) drinking coffee?
examples.chinese: 现在正在喝咖啡的人是谁？

examples.korean: 할 일이 너무 많아서 못 만나요.
examples.english: I have so many things (that I have) to do that I can't meet up.
examples.chinese: 要做的事太多，所以见不了面。

notes: When two or more adjectives are used in succession, only the final adjective is conjugated to the noun modifier form (e.g. 착하고 예쁜 여자를 좋아해요, not 착한 예쁜 여자를 좋아해요).
unit: Unit 18. Changes in Parts of Speech

formation: 동사·형용사 어간 + -기
meaning_en: nominaliser -ing (turns verbs and adjectives into nouns)
meaning_zh: ……（把动词、形容词名词化，相当于“做……这件事”）
meaning_ko: 동사나 형용사를 명사로 바꾸어 주는 표현으로, 문장에서 주어나 목적어 등 여러 성분으로 쓰인다.

examples.english: Studying Korean is difficult.
My hobby is cooking.
My legs hurt, so walking is hard.
My house is far away, so coming to school is difficult.
examples.chinese: 家太远，所以来学校很费劲。

examples.english: Speaking is most difficult.
Wearing it is uncomfortable.

notes: -기 can be combined with a number of particles to form subjects, objects and adverbials in a sentence, e.g. -기(를) 좋아하다/싫어하다, -기(를) 바라다/원하다, -기(를) 시작하다/끝내다/그만두다, -기가 쉽다/어렵다/좋다/편하다/불편하다/힘들다, -기에 좋다/나쁘다.
unit: Unit 18. Changes in Parts of Speech

formation: 형용사 어간 + -게
meaning_en: adverbial '-ly' / 'in a ... manner' (turns adjectives into adverbs)
meaning_zh: ……地（把形容词变成副词，表方式、程度等）
meaning_ko: 형용사 어간에 붙어 문장에서 부사어로 쓰이며, 뒤에 오는 행동의 목적·기준·정도·방법 등을 나타내는 표현이다.

examples.english: I cut my hair short.
I woke up late this morning.
Please read it loudly.

examples.korean: 화장실 청소를 해 주세요. 깨끗하게 해 주세요.
examples.english: Please tidy up the bathroom. Make it clean.
examples.chinese: 请打扫一下卫生间。弄干净一点。

examples.english: I bought it cheap on sale.
It's going to be cold, so dress warmly.

notes: Although the adverbial form of an adjective is made by adding -게 to the stem, in the case of 많다 and 이르다 the forms 많이 and 일찍 are used in favor of 많게 and 이르게. There are also cases in which both the -게 form and a different form are used (빠르다 → 빠르게/빨리, 적다 → 적게/조금, 느리다 → 느리게/천천히).
unit: Unit 18. Changes in Parts of Speech

formation: 형용사 어간 + -아/어하다 (어간 끝 모음이 ㅏ/ㅗ이면 -아하다, 그 외에는 -어하다, 하다이면 -해하다)
meaning_en: appears (to be) / seems (to feel) (turns some adjectives into verbs expressing the subject's feeling or outward appearance)
meaning_zh: 显得……；看起来（表对他人感受或外在表现的观察）
meaning_ko: 일부 형용사에 붙어 동사로 바꾸어, 말하는 사람이 관찰한 느낌이나 겉으로 드러난 모습을 나타내는 표현이다.

examples.english: The children are hungry.
Recently, my father has been tired.
The child is bored.
Budi is afraid of roller coasters.
Yes, they find it amusing.

notes: When adding -지 마세요 to the adjective stem, the pattern becomes -아/어하지 마세요 (e.g. 무서워하지 마세요, not 무섭지 마세요). Also, when -아/어하다 is added to 예쁘다 and 귀엽다 to form 예뻐하다 and 귀여워하다, the meaning becomes 'to hold dear' or 'to treat with love and affection'.
unit: Unit 18. Changes in Parts of Speech

formation: 동사 어간 + -아/어 있다 (어간 끝 모음이 ㅏ/ㅗ이면 -아 있다, 그 외에는 -어 있다, 하다이면 해 있다)
meaning_en: is -ed / is in a -ed state (a continuing state of a completed action)
meaning_zh: ……着（表动作完成后其状态持续，常与被动动词连用）
meaning_ko: 완료된 동작이 계속 유지되는 상태를 나타내는 표현으로, 주로 피동 동사와 함께 쓰인다.

examples.english: The teacher is standing.
The students are sitting.
The patients are lying down in the hospital.
His name is written on the umbrella.
Was there anything inside the wallet?
There was an advertisement put up in front of school.
It's closed.

notes: For verbs meaning to put on or wear, such as 입다, 신다 and 쓰다, -고 있다 is added to the stem to form 입고 있다, 신고 있다 and 쓰고 있다 instead of 입어 있다, 신어 있다 and 써 있다. Also, -아/어 있다 is used only with verbs that do not require a direct object. Compared with -고 있다 (an action currently in progress), -아/어 있다 expresses the continuing state of a completed action.

formation: 형용사 어간 + -아/어지다 (어간 끝 모음이 ㅏ/ㅗ이면 -아지다, 그 외에는 -어지다, 하다이면 해지다)
meaning_en: become / turn (a change in state over time)
meaning_zh: 变得……（表状态随时间发生变化）
meaning_ko: 시간이 지남에 따라 상태가 변함을 나타내는 표현이다.

examples.english: The balloon became bigger.
My elder sister became thinner.
Pinocchio's nose grows longer when he tells a lie.
examples.chinese: 匹诺曹一撒谎鼻子就会变长。

examples.english: It used to be far, but since I've moved, it has become closer.
examples.chinese: 以前很远，但搬家后变近了。

examples.english: After it rained, the weather turned cold.
If you eat a lot of carrots, your vision will get better.
examples.chinese: 多吃胡萝卜的话，视力会变好。

notes: This expression is always used with adjectives and cannot be used with verbs (e.g. 요코 씨가 예뻐졌습니다 O; 요코 씨가 한국말을 잘해졌습니다 X → 잘하게 되었습니다 O). The past tense form -아/어졌어요 expresses a change resulting from an action performed in the past, while the present tense form -아/어져요 is used to describe a change that generally occurs when a particular action is performed.

formation: 동사 어간 + -게 되다
meaning_en: to come to / to become / to end up doing (a change of state or situation, often not by the subject's own will)
meaning_zh: 变得……；逐渐……；结果……（表状态或情况发生变化，常与主语意志无关）
meaning_ko: 어떤 상태나 상황이 다른 사람의 행동이나 환경 때문에 주어의 의지와 상관없이 변하게 되었음을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I became good at cooking.
I came to like soccer.
(It's been decided) I will go abroad on a business trip.
examples.chinese: （结果定下来）我要去国外出差了。

examples.korean: 회사에 다닌 후부터 일찍 일어나게 되었어요.
examples.english: After starting to work at a company, I came to get up early.
examples.chinese: 自从在公司上班以后，我就变得早起了。

examples.korean: 한국에 오기 전에는 몰랐는데 한국에 와서 알게 되었어요.
examples.english: I hadn't heard of him before coming to Korea, but after coming here, I came to know of him.
examples.chinese: 来韩国之前我不知道，来韩国之后才认识了他。

formation: 형용사 어간 + -(으)ㄴ지 / 동사 어간 + -는지 (과거 -았/었는지, 미래 -(으)ㄹ 건지)
meaning_en: whether / what / where / when / how (a clause of unknown or uncertain information, before verbs like 알다/모르다)
meaning_zh: 是否……；……（表不确定或需要确认的内容，接在알다/모르다等词前）
meaning_ko: 알고 싶거나 확실하지 않은 내용을 뒤의 동사에 연결할 때 쓰는 표현으로, '무엇/어디/언제/어떻게/인지'에 해당한다.

examples.english: Do you know how to get to Myeongdong?
I don't know who that person is.

examples.korean: 어제 무엇을 했는지 생각이 안 나요.
examples.english: I can't remember what I did yesterday.
examples.chinese: 我想不起来昨天做了什么。

examples.english: Do you know what's wrong (where it hurts)?
examples.chinese: 你知道（他）哪里不舒服吗？

examples.english: Please tell me how you made this.
examples.chinese: 请告诉我这个是怎么做的。

notes: -는지 is used in the following forms: (1) Interrogative + V-(으)ㄴ/는지, e.g. 우리 아이가 방에서 무엇을 하는지 모르겠어요; (2) V1-(으)ㄴ/는지 V2-(으)ㄴ/는지, e.g. 우리 아이가 방에서 자는지 공부하는지 모르겠어요; (3) V-(으)ㄴ/는지 안 V-(으)ㄴ/는지, e.g. 우리 아이가 공부를 하는지 안 하는지 모르겠어요.

formation: 동사 어간 + -는 데 걸리다/들다
meaning_en: to take (time) / to cost (money) to do something
meaning_zh: 做……需要（花费）……（表做某事所需的时间、金钱或努力）
meaning_ko: 어떤 일을 하는 데 필요한 시간이나 돈, 노력의 양을 나타내는 표현.

examples.korean: 운전을 배우는 데 두 달 걸렸어요.
examples.english: It took (me) two months to learn to drive.
It takes (me) an hour to finish my homework.
It cost (me) 300,000 won to repair my car.

examples.korean: 여기에서 명동까지 가는 데 얼마나 걸려요?
examples.english: How long does it take to get to Myeongdong from here?
examples.chinese: 从这里到明洞需要多长时间？

examples.english: How much did it cost to move?

formation: 형용사/동사 어간 + -지요? (과거 -았/었지요?, 미래 -(으)ㄹ 거지요?, 준말 -죠?)
meaning_en: isn't it? / aren't you? / don't you? (confirming or seeking agreement about something already known)
meaning_zh: ……吧？；不是吗？（表对已知事实的确认或征求同意）
meaning_ko: 이미 알고 있는 사실을 상대방에게 확인하거나 동의를 구할 때 쓰는 표현.

examples.english: You're Chinese, right?
Isn't bulgogi tasty?
You study Korean, don't you?
Doesn't time just fly by?
You'll attend the meeting tomorrow, won't you?

formation: 형용사 어간 + -군요 / 동사 어간 + -는군요 (명사 + (이)군요, 과거 -았/었군요)
meaning_en: I see (that) / indeed / how ...! (expressing surprise or wonder at newly learned information)
meaning_zh: 原来……啊；真是……啊（表对新得知的事实感到惊讶或感叹）
meaning_ko: 직접 보거나 경험하거나 다른 사람에게 들은 새로운 사실에 대해 놀라움이나 감탄을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: Your vision is bad indeed.
You really like ice cream!
I see you've caught a cold.
Budi really does have a lot of money!

examples.korean: 정말 비가 오는군요, 우산이 없는데 어떻게 하죠?
examples.english: Wow, it's really raining; I don't have an umbrella, so what shall I do?
examples.chinese: 真的在下雨啊，我没带伞，该怎么办好呢？

notes: In the informal plain style, -군요 changes to -구나/-군 in the case of adjectives, -는구나/-는군 in the case of verbs, and -(이)구나/(이)군 in the case of nouns.

formation: 형용사/동사 어간 + -네요 (명사 + (이)네요)
meaning_en: really / certainly / wow (expressing surprise or agreement based on direct experience)
meaning_zh: 真是……啊；的确……（表基于亲身体验的惊讶、感叹或对对方话语的认同）
meaning_ko: 직접 경험한 사실에 대한 놀라움이나 감탄, 또는 상대방의 말에 동의할 때 쓰는 표현.

examples.english: Wow, it's already summer.
You certainly have a large family.
You really have good handwriting.
You really have read a lot of books.
Your husband is really tall.
What a beautiful scarf! Thank you.

notes: -군요 is used mostly in books and other written texts and expresses surprise or wonder upon learning something new either by direct experience or by hearing about it from someone else. -네요 is used mostly in daily conversation and cannot be used to express something not learned directly by the speaker's own experience. (Compare with Unit 21, A/V-군요/는군요.)

formation: 형용사 어간 + -(으)ㄴ가요? / 동사 어간 + -나요? (과거 -았/었나요?, 미래 -(으)ㄹ 건가요?)
meaning_en: is/are ...? did ...? (a polite and gentle question)
meaning_zh: ……吗？（表礼貌、柔和的提问）
meaning_ko: 상대방에게 공손하고 부드럽게 질문할 때 쓰는 표현.

examples.english: Do you have a lot of Korean friends?
Do you love me?
Did you have a pleasant weekend?
Do you have time today?
Are you busy these days?

formation: 형용사 어간 + -(으)ㄴ데요 / 동사 어간 + -는데요 (명사 + 인데요, 과거 -았/었는데요)
meaning_en: well, in my case ... / but ... / I'm surprised that ... (mild disagreement, awaiting a response, or surprise)
meaning_zh: 可是……；不过……；真是……啊（表委婉的反驳、等待回应或对意外情况的惊讶）
meaning_ko: 상대방의 말에 부드럽게 반대하거나, 대답을 기다리거나, 예상 밖의 사실에 놀람을 나타내는 표현.

examples.english: I think it's interesting.
Minu is not at his desk right now.
We're really high up!
Well, tomorrow I don't have any time.
Wow, it's really nice.

formation: 인용문 + 하고/라고 + 말하다/물어보다/생각하다/쓰다 등
meaning_en: direct quotation (word-for-word quoting with quotation marks, followed by 하고/라고)
meaning_zh: 直接引语（用引号逐字引用，后接하고/라고）
meaning_ko: 말이나 글, 생각을 그대로 인용 부호와 함께 옮길 때 쓰는 표현으로, 인용문 뒤에 하고/라고를 쓴다.

examples.english: To paraphrase Edison, "Failure is the mother of success."
examples.chinese: 爱迪生说："失败是成功之母。"

examples.english: Jesus said, "Love each other."

examples.korean: 왕징 씨는 저에게 "내일 몇 시에 와요?" 하고 물어봤어요.
examples.english: Wang Jing asked me, "What time will you come tomorrow?"

examples.korean: 부디 씨는 "문제가 너무 어려워." 하고 생각했어요.
examples.english: "This problem is too hard," Budi thought.

examples.korean: 민우 씨가 "요즘 너무 바빠서 만날 수 없어요."라고 그랬어요.
examples.english: Minu said, "I've been too busy recently to be able to meet you."
examples.chinese: 珉宇说："最近太忙了，见不了面。"

notes: 하고 했어요 is not used after a quotation when the part inside the quotation marks ends in 하다, and it is common practice to avoid using 하다 as the verb directly following 하고, because it sounds awkward when 하다 is repeated consecutively. Also, 하고 conveys not just the cited text but also the original intonation, emotion, and feeling (used in fairy tales, children's stories, and onomatopoeia), while 라고 is used often in everyday conversations and speech.

formation: 인용 내용 + -고 하다 (평서 -다고, 의문 -냐고, 청유 -자고, 명령 -(으)라고)
meaning_en: indirect quotation (reporting speech or thought without quotation marks, using -다고/-냐고/-자고/-(으)라고 하다)
meaning_zh: 间接引语（不用引号转述话语或想法，依句型使用-다고/-냐고/-자고/-(으)라고 하다）
meaning_ko: 말이나 글, 생각을 인용 부호 없이 전달할 때 쓰는 표현으로, 인용의 종류에 따라 -다고/-냐고/-자고/-(으)라고 하다를 쓴다.

examples.korean: 민우 씨가 저에게 정말 아름답다고 했어요.
examples.english: Minu said I was really beautiful.
Hayeong said she loves me.
Minu said we should get married.

examples.korean: 제이슨 씨가 오면 식당으로 오라고 전해 주세요.
examples.english: When Jason gets here, please tell him to come to the cafeteria.
examples.chinese: 杰森来了的话，请转告他去食堂。

examples.english: My friends who have tried it said it was delicious.

notes: When indirect quotations are made from sentences that originally end in 주세요 or -아/어 주세요, these parts change to 달라고 하다 and -아/어 달라고 하다, or 주라고 하다 and -아/어 주라고 하다, respectively. 달라고 하다/-아/어 달라고 하다 is used when the speaker makes the request directly to the listener, while 주라고 하다/-아/어 주라고 하다 is used when the speaker asks the listener to help a third party. Also, when the first-person pronoun 나/내 or 저/제 appears inside an indirect quotation, it changes to 자기.

formation: -다고 해요→-대요 / -냐고 해요→-냬요 / -자고 해요→-재요 / -(으)라고 해요→-(으)래요
meaning_en: contracted indirect quotation (colloquial short forms such as -대요/-냬요/-재요/-래요)
meaning_zh: 间接引语缩略形（口语中常用的-대요/-냬요/-재요/-래요等形式）
meaning_ko: 간접 인용을 줄여서 일상 대화에서 자주 쓰는 표현으로, -대요/-냬요/-재요/-래요 등의 형태가 있다.

examples.english: Yoko said Korean is interesting.
Tluen said she's getting married next month.
examples.chinese: 蒂鲁恩说她下个月结婚。

examples.english: Wesley said to call this evening.

examples.korean: 재준 씨는 내일 같이 테니스를 치재요.
examples.english: Jaejun said we should play tennis tomorrow.
examples.chinese: 在俊说我们明天一起打网球吧。

examples.english: Budi wants to know what (you) want to eat.
He said he's been studying Korean.

examples.korean: 유키 씨가 숙제를 좀 도와 달래요.
examples.english: Yuki said she wants help on her homework.
examples.chinese: 由纪说让我帮她做作业。

formation: 어간 끝 'ㅡ' + '아/어'로 시작하는 어미 → 'ㅡ' 탈락 (예: 바쁘다→바빠요, 예쁘다→예뻐서)
meaning_en: the 'ㅡ' irregular conjugation: ㅡ is dropped before endings beginning with 아/어
meaning_zh: 'ㅡ'不规则活用：词干以ㅡ结尾时，后接아/어开头的词尾，ㅡ脱落
meaning_ko: 어간이 'ㅡ'로 끝나는 형용사와 동사에 '아/어'로 시작하는 어미가 붙을 때 'ㅡ'가 탈락하는 불규칙 활용.

examples.english: Minu is really busy these days.
Please turn off the lights.
I'm hungry.
I'm crying because the movie was so sad.
examples.chinese: 电影太悲伤了，我正在哭。

examples.english: The weather was bad, so I couldn't go on the picnic.
examples.chinese: 天气不好，所以没能去郊游。

formation: 어간 끝 'ㄹ' + 'ㄴ/ㅂ/ㅅ'로 시작하는 어미 → 'ㄹ' 탈락 (예: 살다→삽니다, 만들다→만드세요)
meaning_en: the 'ㄹ' irregular conjugation: ㄹ is dropped before endings beginning with ㄴ, ㅂ, or ㅅ
meaning_zh: 'ㄹ'不规则活用：词干以ㄹ结尾时，后接ㄴ/ㅂ/ㅅ开头的词尾，ㄹ脱落
meaning_ko: 어간이 'ㄹ'로 끝나는 동사와 형용사에 'ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ'으로 시작하는 어미가 붙을 때 'ㄹ'이 탈락하는 불규칙 활용.

examples.english: The girl plays well by herself.

examples.korean: 백화점이 몇 시에 여는지 알고 싶어요.
examples.english: I'd like to know what time the department store opens.
examples.chinese: 我想知道百货商店几点开门。

examples.english: What are you making?

examples.korean: 전자 사전을 어디에서 싸게 파는지 아세요?
examples.english: Do you know where I can get an electronic dictionary for a good price?
examples.chinese: 你知道哪里有卖便宜的电子词典吗？

examples.korean: 우리 집은 머니까 학교 다니기 힘들어요.
examples.english: Our house is far from school, so it's hard to commute.
examples.chinese: 我家离学校远，所以上学很辛苦。

notes: When -(으)ㄹ is added to stems ending in ㄹ, such as -(으)ㄹ 때, -(으)게요, and -(으)ㄹ 래요?, ㄹ is omitted and the stem attaches directly to the ending. e.g. 살다 + -(으)ㄹ 때 → 살 때; 만들다 + -(으)ㄹ 래요? → 만들래요?

formation: 어간 끝 'ㅂ' + 모음으로 시작하는 어미 → '우'로 변함 (돕다/곱다는 '오'로 변함)
meaning_en: the 'ㅂ' irregular conjugation: ㅂ changes to 우 (or 오) before vowel endings
meaning_zh: 'ㅂ'不规则活用：词干以ㅂ结尾时，后接元音开头的词尾，ㅂ变为우（돕다/곱다变为오）
meaning_ko: 어간이 'ㅂ'으로 끝나는 동사와 형용사에 모음으로 시작하는 어미가 붙을 때 'ㅂ'이 '우'로 바뀌는 불규칙 활용('돕다/곱다'는 '오'로 바뀜).

examples.english: The coffee is hot, so be careful.
It's cold outside, so I stayed home.
examples.chinese: 天气冷，所以我待在家里了。

examples.english: I like spicy food.
What kind of movies do you like?
The food is a little bland, so could I have some salt?

notes: 돕다 (to assist) and 곱다 (lovely/charming) are the only two words that change ㅂ to 오; all others change to 우. Although the stems of 좁다, 입다, 씹다, and 잡다 end in ㅂ, they are conjugated regularly.

formation: 어간 끝 'ㄷ' + 모음으로 시작하는 어미 → 'ㄹ'로 변함 (예: 듣다→들어요, 묻다→물어요, 걷다→걸어요)
meaning_en: the 'ㄷ' irregular conjugation: ㄷ changes to ㄹ before vowel endings
meaning_zh: 'ㄷ'不规则活用：部分词干以ㄷ结尾的动词后接元音开头的词尾时，ㄷ变为ㄹ
meaning_ko: 일부 어간이 'ㄷ'으로 끝나는 동사에 모음으로 시작하는 어미가 붙을 때 'ㄷ'이 'ㄹ'로 바뀌는 불규칙 활용.

examples.english: I listen to music while I exercise.
examples.chinese: 我一边听音乐一边运动。

examples.english: I had no money, so I went by foot.
I asked her for her phone number.
examples.chinese: 我问了那个女人的电话号码。

examples.korean: 날씨가 좋은데 밖에 나가서 좀 걸을까요?
examples.english: The weather's nice, so why don't we go for a walk outside?
examples.chinese: 天气很好，我们出去散散步怎么样？

examples.korean: 이 노래 들어 봤어요? 정말 좋아요.
examples.english: Have you heard this song? It's really good.
examples.chinese: 你听过这首歌吗？真的很好。

notes: Although the stems of 닫다 (to close), 받다 (to receive), and 믿다 (to believe) end in ㄷ, they are conjugated regularly.

formation: 어간 끝 '르' + '아/어'로 시작하는 어미 → 'ㅡ' 탈락 + 'ㄹ' 덧남 (예: 다르다→달라요, 부르다→불러요)
meaning_en: the '르' irregular conjugation: ㅡ is dropped and ㄹ is added before 아/어 endings
meaning_zh: '르'不规则活用：词干以르结尾时，后接아/어开头的词尾，ㅡ脱落并添加ㄹ
meaning_ko: 어간이 '르'로 끝나는 동사와 형용사에 '아/어'로 시작하는 어미가 붙을 때 'ㅡ'가 탈락하고 'ㄹ'이 덧나는 불규칙 활용.

examples.korean: 댄 씨는 노래를 잘 불러서 인기가 많아요.
examples.english: Dane is popular because he can sing well.
examples.chinese: 丹很会唱歌，所以很受欢迎。

examples.english: The subway is faster than the bus during rush hour.
examples.chinese: 上班时间地铁比公交车快。

examples.english: I don't speak English.
Did you cut your hair? It's stylish.
Their personalities are very different too.

formation: 어간 끝 'ㅎ' + 모음으로 시작하는 어미 → 'ㅎ' 탈락 (아/어 계열은 'ㅐ'로 변함, 예: 하얗다→하얀/하얘요)
meaning_en: the 'ㅎ' irregular conjugation: ㅎ is dropped before vowel endings (and the 아/어 ending becomes ㅐ)
meaning_zh: 'ㅎ'不规则活用：词干以ㅎ结尾的形容词后接元音开头的词尾时，ㅎ脱落（아/어类词尾变为ㅐ）
meaning_ko: 어간이 'ㅎ'으로 끝나는 형용사에 모음으로 시작하는 어미가 붙을 때 'ㅎ'이 탈락하는 불규칙 활용.

examples.english: Snow White has black hair and a white complexion.
examples.chinese: 白雪公主头发乌黑，皮肤白皙。

examples.korean: 왕비는 백설 공주에게 빨간 사과를 줬어요.
examples.english: The queen gave Snow White a red apple.
examples.chinese: 王后给了白雪公主一个红苹果。

examples.korean: 왕자는 크고 파란 눈으로 공주를 봤어요.
examples.english: The prince looked at Snow White with his big blue eyes.
examples.chinese: 王子用又大又蓝的眼睛看着公主。

examples.english: The autumn sky is really blue.

examples.korean: 하늘은 파랗고 구름은 하애서 그림 같아요.
examples.english: The sky is blue and the clouds are white, just like a painting.
examples.chinese: 天空湛蓝，云朵洁白，就像一幅画。

notes: When the stems of 이렇다, 그렇다, 저렇다, and 어떻다 are added to endings that begin with -아/어, they conjugate to 이래, 그래, 저래, and 어때 instead of 이레, 그레, 저레, and 어레. Also, although the stems of 좋다, 많다, 낳다, and 넣다 end in ㅎ, they are conjugated regularly.

formation: 어간 끝 'ㅅ' + 모음으로 시작하는 어미 → 'ㅅ' 탈락 (예: 짓다→지어요, 낫다→나아요)
meaning_en: the 'ㅅ' irregular conjugation: ㅅ is dropped before vowel endings
meaning_zh: 'ㅅ'不规则活用：部分词干以ㅅ结尾时，后接元音开头的词尾，ㅅ脱落
meaning_ko: 일부 어간이 'ㅅ'으로 끝나는 동사와 형용사에 모음으로 시작하는 어미가 붙을 때 'ㅅ'이 탈락하는 불규칙 활용.

examples.english: A mosquito bit me, so my eye became swollen.

examples.korean: 컵에 커피와 크림, 설탕을 넣고 저어요.
examples.english: I put coffee, cream, and sugar in the cup and stir it all together.
examples.chinese: 在杯子里放入咖啡、奶油和糖，然后搅拌。

examples.english: Which outfit is better?
Who named your child?
Did you get over your cold?

notes: In Korean, vowels often combine when they meet (e.g. 배우 + -어요 → 배워요). However, in the case of irregular ㅅ stems, even though vowels may meet after the ㅅ is deleted, they do not combine. e.g. 짓다 + -어요 → 지어요 (O) / 저요 (X); 낫다 + -아요 → 나아요 (O) / 나요 (X). Also, although the stems of 벗다, 웃다, and 씻다 end in ㅅ, they are conjugated regularly.
